text:
sam: Heads-up — I'm proposing a small but important change to runtime config gating for routing policies. Current problem: our percent-rollout only applies to the *primary* routing rule, which makes testing cost-based fallbacks awkward.

maria: Can you sketch the scenario? I missed the demo earlier. :eyes:

sam: Example: tenant A should go to low-cost variant (q4-quant) 30% and default model otherwise. But when low-cost is unavailable we currently fall back to default without honoring the original rollout percentage in the control plane. That means we lose the canary signal.

kevin: Right — we want the rollouts to be deterministic wrt policy evaluation not availability. Otherwise metrics (latency/cost/quality) are biased.

alex: Are you proposing a change to the rollout semantics or to the routing engine? Two options: 1) evaluate the percentage first and then pick a route (even if it ends up unavailable, trigger fallback but keep metrics tagged) or 2) keep evaluation but add telemetry tags indicating "intended_variant" vs "served_variant".

sam: Thinking both. Minimal change: add two fields to the runtime config for a route: "intent_tag" (string) and "preserve_intent_on_fallback" (bool). Default false. If true, obs pipeline must record intended_variant.

maria: That sounds safe. Telemetry change needs a small schema update but non-breaking. How would the config look?

sam: Example config snippet: 

```yaml
routes:
  - name: low_cost_canary
    variant: q4-quant
    rollout_percent: 30
    intent_tag: "canary_q4"
    preserve_intent_on_fallback: true
```

kevin: Looks good. A few notes: 1) we'll need a migration for existing dashboards that aggregate by variant if we add intent_tag. 2) For quota accounting we must decide whether quota charges go to served_variant (obvious) or to intended_variant (we should keep billing tied to served to avoid surprises).

alex: +1 on billing tied to served_variant. But we should emit both fields so post-agg can compute cost-per-intended if needed.

maria: UX question for the Console: how to represent this in rollout UI? We currently show a single slider for percent. If we add intent preservation we need to surface that fallback will not collapse the canary. Maybe a toggle with small help text.

sam: Agreed. Proposed console copy: "Preserve intended variant on fallback — when enabled, telemetry will record which variant was selected by rollout logic even if runtime fallback served another variant." Small tooltip about billing.

kevin: Also we should guard this behind an org-level flag for a week to watch for unintended explodes in metrics cardinality. I can add a temp flag in runtime-config: `allow_intent_tags`.

maria: Can we do a quick experiment without a platform rollout? Maybe wire it to a single test org (redwood-internal) so we can validate end-to-end?

sam: Yes — plan: implement config field + telemetry tag emission behind `allow_intent_tags` plus a console toggle that only shows if org in test list. Deploy to staging, exercise with canary traffic generator.

alex: Who will own changes in observability? We need: metric schema (labels), dashboard updates, and log parsers. @obs-bot would you create a ticket?

obs-bot: created OBS-402: "Support intended_variant telemetry label + dashboard refresh" (link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/OBS-402) :white_check_mark:

kevin: I'll own the runtime change and add unit tests. Sam — can you draft a short RFC for the exact semantics (edge cases: multi-stage fallbacks, combined percent+attribute rules)?

sam: Will do. Draft incoming in #arch tomorrow. Quick question: for rollout audits we also need to retain history of the intent_tag used per evaluation. Do we keep that in event log (kafka) or a lightweight span annotation?

maria: Store intent_tag in the event stream (kafka). Spans are ephemeral and sampling could drop the info. We want full fidelity for QA.

alex: Agreed. Also add a compact enum mapping so we don't explode cardinality (e.g., canonicalize common intent tags to small ints).

kevin: Implementation detail: the routing node should annotate the request metadata with `meta.intended_variant` before attempting to pick a backend. Then fallback path reads metadata to emit telemetry.

sam: I'll include pseudo-code in the RFC. Something like: 

```go
// evaluate rollout
intent := chooseByRand(routes)
req.Meta.Set("intended_variant", intent)
backend, err := pickAvailableBackend(intent)
if err != nil {
  backend = pickFallback()
  req.Meta.Set("served_variant", backend.variant)
}
emitTelemetry(req.Meta)
```

maria: Nice. Last ops concern: make sure SLO alerts don't fire because of labelled experiments — we should tag experiment traffic in dashboards so oncall can mute noisy canaries.

kevin: We'll add an "experiment=true" tag for traffic with rollout_percent < 100 and intent preserved. Console should expose an option to mark a rollout as "experiment" which toggles the label.

sam: Great. Next steps: kevin implements runtime flag behind `allow_intent_tags`, obs team updates pipeline (OBS-402), alex prototypes console toggle with test org gating, sam writes RFC. Target: staging deploy by EOW, prod gated rollouts next week.

maria: Thanks all. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deployed config-service@staging already (build 5521) — watch logs at /deploys/5521

sam: Nice, I'll start the RFC now and ping the thread when it's up.
